lines.text: Every FRC field comes with a map. It says exactly where each field element, and each AprilTag on it, should be.
But real fields are built by people, at every event. The real element usually sits a little off its spot on the map.
The field drawings allow half an inch and one degree, and FIRST has warned that real events can be worse.
Our robot's job: stop on the real scoring spot, within two centimeters and one degree. About the width of your thumb.
Here's the catch. Even a robot that knows exactly where it is would drive to where the element should be, not where it is.
In our simulator, driving to the map spot hits the target fifty seven percent of the time. On messier fields, thirty one, then fifteen.
So near the target, our robot stops trusting the map. It measures the target itself, using the AprilTag stuck on it.
With everything in this video switched on, the same simulator scores one hundred, ninety nine, and ninety eight percent.
We'll go in five steps: the goal, the idea in plain words, the maths with real numbers, the Java code, and a recap.
